speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) in each of the last five years, how many requests have been received to waive the additional levy payable by vehicle owners who transfer their vehicles between the fourth and sixth month from the date of registration; (b) how many requests for waiver have been granted; and (c) what are the main reasons for such waivers to be granted.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Ministry has assessed the effectiveness of the imposition of an additional levy on cars sold between the fourth and sixth month of ownership in discouraging COE speculation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If cars are transferred between four and six months from the date of registration, an additional levy would be payable if the Quota Premium (QP) of the corresponding COE category at the point of transfer is higher than the original QP paid upon successful bidding for the COE.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The additional levy is part of a suite of measures to discourage COE speculation, which also includes requiring a bid deposit and disallowing the transfer of Temporary COEs (TCOEs) for Cat A and Cat B vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over the same period, only one request to transfer car ownership from a deceased person to the executor of the deceased estate was acceded to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Just to follow up quickly on the original question in the Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am wondering if Senior Minister of State Amy Khor would elaborate on whether the efforts at discouraging speculation along the lines of banning transfers between four and six months have been relatively more effective than other kinds of measures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: For instance, right now, my understanding is that lots of COEs are being speculated on indirectly by those that are purchased during a high supply year and then subsequently resold it in a low supply year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, let me clarify that for vehicle transfers within four to six months of registration is not a ban on transfer.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You just need to pay the additional levy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the question about whether this is an effective policy tool, I have said in my reply earlier that it is part of a suite of measures to discourage COE speculation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: By way of explanation, let me also say that this policy to discourage double transfers was first implemented in 1995.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is really to discourage double transfers whereby you may bypass, to this means, the non-transfer TCOE policy of Cat A and Cat B vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And there were public sentiments that double transfers would have resulted in higher COE prices.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the first three months, you are not allowed to transfer for Cat A and Cat B vehicles and then, subsequently, in the next three months, you can transfer, but you will need to pay an additional levy only if what you paid is actually lower than the QP at the point of transfer, otherwise, there would not be any additional levy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If you look at the numbers, I have said that, over the last five years, we received, on average, about three appeals for a waiver of the additional levy.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I am just also wondering whether it is possible that LTA would consider cases where there is a very sudden, unexpected and catastrophic event, something like a permanent disability to the car owner or within the family, whether or not that would also qualify for waiver of the additional levy, because, sometimes, we do not plan it, especially when we are at a relatively young age.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: But, of course, the additional waiver can be quite a significant burden on this household which is already struggling and having to deal with this permanent disability or long-term illness.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, this is part of a suite of policy tools to discourage double-transfer COE speculation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, for this to remain useful and relevant, the conditions or circumstances under which waiver of the additional levy can be given would necessarily need to be stringent and limited in terms of circumstances.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, as I have earlier clarified, the additional levy policy just means that if you want to transfer within four to six months, you have to pay an additional levy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And for vehicle owners who wish to transfer within the four to six months and not wait thereafter because of various circumstances, they can actually sell it to motorcar dealers registered with LTA – what we called the electronic service agents – whereby they will not need to bear the additional levy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, these registered dealers can take temporary ownership without incurring an actual transfer count and they have 12 months to sell the vehicle.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And if they actually sell it after six months of vehicle registration, they also do not need to pay additional levy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, there is a way out, an option, for the appellant.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, we hear the Member's views.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And let me say that we will continue to look at appeals and review the circumstances under which waivers can be granted, where the conditions warrant such a waiver.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I just want to ask one last clarification from the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: I am just wondering whether, in terms of awareness of this scheme, this is something that LTA actually tells people who ask for this, because I just do not think that many people out there are aware that this is possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I am also aware that the Member has an appeal case on this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And our advice would usually be that they should approach CaseTrust- Singapore Vehicle Traders Association-accredited dealers for such an option.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I am wondering if the Senior Minister of State will clarify that, indeed, the Ministry's assessment of the efficacy of this particular additional levy scheme in discouraging speculation is based on the low number of transfers that are being transacted as a result of this scheme.
